title: Sweet potatoes, orange flesh, without skin, raw

content.title: About
content.content: Sweet potatoes (batata) with orange flesh, peeled and raw are a root vegetable rich in carbohydrates, vitamins, and minerals. They have a sweet taste, firm texture, and bright orange color due to high beta‑carotene content.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Sweet potatoes belong to the Convolvulaceae family and are not related to regular potatoes.
The orange flesh indicates a high level of provitamin A (beta‑carotene).
Batata can be grown in tropical, subtropical, and even temperate regions with proper conditions.
There are several varieties: orange, yellow, white, and even purple-fleshed sweet potatoes.
Raw sweet potatoes are often used in salads, pickles, and as an ingredient in juices.

items.title: Rich in beta‑carotene
items.content: Beta‑carotene converts to vitamin A in the body, supporting vision, immunity, and skin health.

items.title: Source of dietary fiber
items.content: Fiber aids digestion, promotes satiety, and helps regulate blood sugar levels.

items.title: Contains vitamin C
items.content: Vitamin C enhances antioxidant protection and participates in collagen synthesis.

items.title: Minerals: potassium and magnesium
items.content: Potassium supports fluid balance, while magnesium is important for muscle and nerve function.

items.title: Moderate glycemic index when cooked
items.content: Raw sweet potatoes have a moderate glycemic index, which decreases further when baked, making them suitable for blood‑sugar management.

items.title: Allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience an allergic reaction to sweet potatoes.

items.title: Oxalate content
items.content: Raw sweet potatoes contain oxalates, which can contribute to kidney stone formation in susceptible people.

items.title: Digestive discomfort
items.content: Large amounts of raw sweet potato may cause gas and stomach upset.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Raw sweet potatoes can be sliced thinly for salads, juiced, or used in pickles. They are also grated for raw vegetable dishes.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store sweet potatoes in a cool, dry, dark place at 10‑15 °C. Do not refrigerate, as low temperatures can alter flavor and texture. For long‑term storage, check for soft spots or mold.
